agent_trace.summary: Diffuse pleural thickening on a chest X-ray refers to broad, usually bilateral or extensive pleural scarring/thickening along the chest wall, often most visible at the lateral lung bases or apices rather than within the lung parenchyma. In the retrieved similar chest X-ray cases, the answers were not directly specific to pleural thickening, so they mainly reinforce that this is a chest radiograph interpretation task and should be localized to the pleural spaces.

key_facts: Pleural thickening is a pleural, not parenchymal, abnormality and tracks along the inner chest wall.
Diffuse pleural thickening often appears as smooth or irregular pleural opacity, sometimes with blunting of the costophrenic angles.
It may be unilateral or bilateral and is commonly more conspicuous at the lateral lung bases or apices.
Distinguishing pleural thickening from pleural effusion relies on shape and distribution; thickening is more plaque-like or rind-like, while effusion layers or menisci.
Prior infection, inflammation, asbestos exposure, hemothorax, or empyema can lead to pleural thickening.
